findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass the workflow identity through the CLI's `--author-name` / `--author-email` flags (sourced from BRIDGE_BOT_NAME / BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL), not via environment variables the module does not read.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/push.py::_main passes author_name=parsed.author_name, author_email=parsed.author_email; commit_and_push_tickets_branch turns those into `-c user.name=`/`-c user.email=` git args
The module never reads os.environ['BRIDGE_BOT_NAME'] or BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL
Plan RED oracle: 'reconciler workflow ... must commit/push with the workflow-supplied identity'
findings.finding: The plan forwards commit identity via the BRIDGE_BOT_NAME / BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL environment variables, but the `commit-and-push` CLI accepts authorship only through `--author-name` / `--author-email` flags; it reads no such env vars for git author identity. Forwarding them as env alone would drop the workflow-supplied identity from the commit.
findings.location: Approach bullet 1 ('forwarding BRIDGE_BOT_NAME / BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL') and AC 'Reconciler commits retain the configured BRIDGE_BOT_NAME / BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL identity'
scenarios: The commit-and-push call passes identity only via env; the resulting commit uses whatever global git user.* the runner has, not the bridge bot
The identity-preservation acceptance test would need --author-* flags to pass
findings.suggested_fix: In the commit-and-push call add `--author-name "$BRIDGE_BOT_NAME" --author-email "$BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL"`, keeping the env exports only to populate those shell variables.
